claims.statement: Termind is one Xcode project with native `TFM` macOS and `TFI` iPhone/iPad app targets, shared framework targets and separate test, widget, and macOS MCP bridge products; platform UI and lifecycle remain app-owned.

A safe change must preserve the lifetime split: app services are shared, desktop workspaces are window-local, mobile navigation is scene-local, and mobile live workspaces and saved descriptors belong to persistent UIKit scene sessions, not a single cross-window workspace pool.

TermindApp is the macOS composition root: it creates the SwiftData container and app-wide services, uses in-memory storage for tests or screenshot demos, and fails startup rather than silently replacing an unavailable local database.

`TermindIOSApp` migrates language preference and creates one live or testing `MobileAppModel`; `MobileStartupView` injects the model container into successful scenes and shows unavailable data if composition fails.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests enforce root-specific import restrictions: five non-presentation shared frameworks cannot import app targets or AppKit/UIKit/IOKit/ServiceManagement, while Presentation has a separate rule allowing SwiftUI but excluding app targets, native UI, storage and implementation modules; shared Application cannot import Infrastructure, Persistence or SwiftData, and scanned SwiftData model declarations belong in Persistence.

AgentKit is a separately versioned remote package: it owns host-neutral agent runtime behavior, while Termind owns SSH/SFTP tools; cross-repository work requires an AgentKit release followed by a project minimum-version bump and resolved dependency update.
Routine Xcode validation must use `-onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile`; the repository defines TFM/TFI build entrypoints, strict Swift formatting, and a localization validation script.
macOS tests that show windows or take focus are intentionally opt-in through `TEST_RUNNER_TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1` or `TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1`, so routine validation remains headless.

MobileAppModel aggregates scene phases so all scenes must background before it pauses monitoring, memory, sync, metrics and outbox; background-task expiration suspends workspaces, stops forwarding, pauses transfers and expires the Assistant, while an active scene resumes eligible services.

During Debug tests closing the last macOS window does not terminate the test host; otherwise last-window termination requires menu-bar metrics disabled and metrics not keeping the app alive. A quit request rechecks pending SFTP edits and permits cancellation before starting shutdown.

Mac app termination fences new Assistant work, cancels and drains conversations and pending preparations before agent resource closure, while stopping MCP and transfers; AppKit receives one termination reply on cleanup completion or after a three-second fallback.

Each persistent UIKit scene session receives a scene-local navigation and Assistant presentation model plus its own mobile workspace session; MobileAppModel holds shared services and aggregates the sessions, and closing an owned live workspace ends its connection-history entry.
Mobile key-window integration tests require TEST_RUNNER_TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS=1, disabled parallel testing and a narrow TFITests filter.

App copy changes require completed simplified and traditional Chinese translations and the localization script, while language behavior changes use AppLanguageTests and website changes require a production build and English/Chinese route checks.

The Debug macOS test host launches the real app but suppresses automatic main and external-auth windows unless TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1 or a screenshot demo is active; it disables main-scene restoration during tests and screenshot demos, while focus-changing tests independently require a visible-window trait opt-in.

RootView registers each window with the shared AppModel and publishes a focused window value while its own WindowModel owns navigation and workspaces; switching destinations preserves mounted workspace native views.

App-facing copy is shared through TermindPresentation/Strings and manually maintained string catalogs; catalog edits require normalization and both AppStrings and Chinese localization checks, and simplified and traditional Chinese translations must be finished with changed English copy.

MobileAdaptiveLayoutTests is serialized but does not use the mobile UI environment gate, unlike opt-in mobile key-window integration suites; narrow nonparallel runs are appropriate when investigating its process-wide UIKit fixture.
The desktop external-authentication Window receives the shared app environment and SwiftData container but removes its normal Window-menu command; it is not another main workspace window.

Selecting a saved mobile descriptor publishes a live workspace in the owning workspace session before connecting; another scene's activity link routes to that owner rather than creating a duplicate connection, and repeated selection in the owner reuses the same workspace.
Xcode requires remote AgentKit through upToNextMajorVersion from 0.19.0; pinned builds consume the release/revision in Package.resolved, not sibling source edits.

At mobile cold launch, saved workspace records are consolidated into the first bound scene session without reconnecting; the other newly bound scene has no workspaces, and restore failure reports an error rather than letting a second scene claim the same records.

Mobile scene removal or backgrounding does not itself discard workspaces; when a native session disappears reconciliation transfers its live workspaces to an active session without reconnecting, while explicit discard closes the affected workspaces.
Mobile workspace restoration saves descriptors rather than one-shot commands or initial directory paths, so relaunch does not reconnect automatically or replay a snippet.

The mobile startup view waits for the UIKit scene delegate's session ID; MobileBoundSceneRoot creates and retains its scene model in a task rather than during view evaluation, and binds the delegate to the shared app when its root appears.

SSH Security Key registration and signing is owned by the Termind SSH integration, with focused Vault metadata, WebAuthn and interaction-policy tests for its persistence and authentication boundaries.

CloudSyncLifecycle maintains a category-specific engine and account scope, persists a recovery fence before creating an automatically syncing engine, fetches before allowing uploads, and reconciles pending engine changes against the durable journal.

Cloud sync pause, account changes, and non-cancellation failures retire the current engine, fence its operations, and cancel it outside the delegate context; late completions from retired engines cannot update replacement-engine status.

ConnectionJourney owns shared connection progress and authentication/host-key checkpoint state, and shared ConnectionJourneyRouteView draws the route for desktop and mobile while app views supply native surrounding controls; state and mobile rendering can be checked separately from a live SSH connection.

Metrics journey native presentation is exercised by desktop visible-window MetricsJourneyRenderingTests and serialized mobile MobileMetricsJourneyTests, which cover keyboard authentication retained in metrics navigation; mobile metrics tests are not gated by TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS.

Security Key destination and jump credentials resolve from Vault metadata without Keychain, while hardware references persist and sync as external metadata with compatibility normalization; failed metadata writes/deletes roll back and software keys cannot use external storage.

The WebAuthn SSH fixture validates registration parsing, signed assertion fields, security flags, tampering and malformed CBOR, but its synthetic P-256 fixture does not establish physical-key or native system-prompt behavior.

A forbidden SSH interaction policy blocks security-key credentials for both destination and jumps even when user presence is optional, so silent auxiliary connections must not trigger a hardware prompt.
The desktop delegate's three-second fallback bounds the once-only AppKit quit reply, not completion of the asynchronous shutdown task.

The libghostty-spm maintenance checkout is not the app's build source: Xcode selects a versioned remote release, so package changes require updating the fork, submodule gitlink, project minimum version and resolved pin together; native patch changes additionally require an XCFramework release and matching package URL/checksum.

Termind's iOS terminal subclass customizes separate unselected and selected touch-menu hooks, grouping and localizing editing actions before uploads and remaining system items; its macOS terminal adapter instead composes secondary-click menus through AppKit selection/menu hooks. These app seams do not establish package-owned indirect-pointer behavior.

Mobile workspace search binds SSH/Telnet queries and presentation to a workspace-owned TerminalFindController that dispatches Ghostty binding actions, while SFTP search binds directly to sftpChannel.query.

MobileToolbarSearch gives UISearchController ownership of native search presentation, defers synchronization from SwiftUI updates, and blocks text/presentation synchronization during dismissal until UIKit reports completion, preventing dismissal from reopening the search UI.

Native mobile terminal-search dismissal ends Find without requesting terminal focus, and terminal Find queries and SFTP filter queries survive closing and repeated reopening; clearing the query does not itself dismiss the search UI.

Mobile workspace journey presentation keeps the search modifier outside journey-dependent content and retains the terminal surface mounted but hidden and noninteractive; the opt-in serialized MobileTerminalSearchIntegrationTests checks retained search-controller identity for SSH/SFTP and attached terminal identity for SSH across journey presentation.
The live SwiftData schema is V51, adding Snippet color over a frozen historical model; SnippetColorTests verifies real V50 migration, color persistence and reopening independently of wire versions.
Snippet wire records read V1/V2 and write V2, independently of the V51 local schema; HostGroup/SSHKey use V3 writers and historical readers.
Mobile scene Workspace/Transfers destinations and Connection Picker/Batch Startup sheets each use one optional enum with derived compatibility accessors, preventing competing stored routes.
Terminal Find resize suspension retains query/presentation, suppresses engine search/navigation, and resumes only the latest still-presented nonempty query.
